subject: [PATCH] x86/lib: Use REP MOVSB for large memcpy() on ERMS CPUs without FSRM

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about code readability and suggested moving the check to memcpy_orig() after a 32-byte compare.

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Proposed an alternative implementation that eliminates nop instructions and moves ERMS logic to memcpy_orig().
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, 20 Oct 2026 at 23:55, Kiryl Shutsemau <kas@kernel.org> wrote:
>
> Moving MOVQ inside ALTERNATIVE_2 is ugly...

Yeah, maybe it would make sense to make that function be

        movq %rdi, %rax
        movq %rdx, %rcx
        ALTERNATIVE "jmp memcpy_orig", "rep movsb", X86_FEATURE_FSRM
        RET

instead? No nop instructions at all, and both alternatives are two bytes.

Then do any ERMS logic at the top of memcpy_orig, which now has the
registers ready for string instructions anyway.

Hmm?

                      Linus

2026-10-21.patch_summary: Patch proposes using REP MOVSB for large memcpy() on ERMS CPUs without FSRM, but Kiryl Shutsemau raises concerns about code readability and Linus Torvalds suggests an alternative implementation.
